  "elsewhere_quote": "A(y,x) &= (x-y)^2 - c^2 - 2c(x+y) \\ge 0 \\;\\Longrightarrow\\; (x-y)^2 \\ge c^2 + 2c(x+y). \\tag{11}\n\\end{aligned}\n\\]\n\nFrom (11) and $x,y>0$ we obtain $(x-y)^2 > c^2$, hence  \n\n\\[\n|x-y| > c \\qquad \\forall\\,x\\in S_0,\\;y\\in S_c . \\tag{12}",
  "status_as_written": "false_display",
  "repair_distance": "symbol",
  "explanation": "The general formula gives A(x,y) = (x-y)^2 - a^2 - 2a(x+y) + 4by + 2b^2, so with a=0, b=c the term is +4cy, not +4cx; the objection's local claim is correct. But that line is inert: it only records that A(x,y) >= 0 holds trivially and is never used. The separation |x-y| > c (the content of L5.5 needed here) comes from (11), i.e. A(y,x) = (x-y)^2 - c^2 - 2c(x+y) >= 0, which is correctly expanded (a=c, b=0), and from B(x,y) = (x-y)^2 - 4cx in (10), also correct. Hence a one-symbol misprint beside a valid argument.",
  "objection_severity": "cosmetic"
}
